title: Token floodgate and fallback coordinator for multi-region bursts
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Design and implement a lightweight 'floodgate' component that sits in front of existing token limiters to absorb short bursts, maintain proportional fairness across tenants, and coordinate safe failover between regions when local limiters become unavailable. The floodgate provides a bounded burst buffer, per-tenant slope limiting, and a soft-lease protocol for cross-region fallback. Primary goal: keep tail latency and SLO violations low during regional limiter outages and traffic spikes while preserving predictable unit economics.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy floodgate as sidecar/edge service with <10ms median additional latency on p95 request path under normal load

During simulated local limiter outage, floodgate successfully shifts eligible requests to fallback region within configured soft-lease timeout and maintains per-tenant fairness (no tenant gets >2x share of aggregate short burst limit)
Observed SLO impact: p99 latency increase <10% and error rate increase <=0.5% for standard workloads during failover tests
Operational runbooks created: rollback, emergency disable, and metrics/alert thresholds documented
Integration tests added: deterministic token-lattice unit tests and multi-region chaos test that simulates network partition and limiter crash
implementation_notes: Floodgate components are purely in-memory and maintain a small bounded queue per token bucket with configurable max_burst_tokens
Use a token-lattice allocator: allocate burst tokens proportional to recent steady-state usage over a sliding window (default 60s) to preserve fairness across tenants
Soft-lease protocol: when local limiter is unresponsive for X ms, request a soft lease from remote coordinator; lease duration short (eg. 3s) and renewable to avoid long cross-region ownership
Circuit breaker thresholds derive from SLO signals (latency/errorbudget burn). When circuit trips, floodgate rejects non-critical traffic and prioritizes high-tier tenants based on weight table
Telemetry: emit per-tenant burst_consumed, lease_granted, lease_rejected, failover_count, queued_ms percentiles; tag metrics with region and limiter_state
Backward compatibility: floodgate uses header-based opt-in gating and feature-flag rollout per service team
tradeoffs: Pros: reduced SLO impact on short bursts and clearer cross-region handoff semantics
Cons: increased system complexity and potential for cross-region amplification if leases are too generous
Staleness: fairness decisions rely on recent usage windows and can transiently favor bursty tenants; smoothing window size is tunable
Cost: extra network/compute during failover when routing to remote region; include cost metrics to monitor economics
rollout: Phase 1 (canary): deploy floodgate opt-in to 5% of traffic in us-west with feature flag; monitor p95/p99 latency and reject rates for 72h
Phase 2 (regional expansion): enable in two regions with soft-lease disabled; compare against baseline for burst absorption effectiveness
Phase 3 (coordinator on): enable soft-lease/coordinator; run controlled limiter crash experiments in staging and measure cross-region traffic amplification
Phase 4 (gradual ramp): increase to 50% then 100% while enabling automatic fallback policies and runbook handoffs
Include kill-switch that immediately disables floodgate routing and clears queues without changing upstream limiter config
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Mehta: Initial sketch reviewed with SRE and Runtime teams. Concerns raised about lease durations causing cross-region token duplication; proposed short leases and renewable tokens.
2026-03-05 - Luis Ortega: Prototype of per-tenant burst queues shows median enqueue/dequeue cost <500ns in Go; will add additional profiling under high concurrency.
2026-03-08 - Priya Nair (SRE): Suggest adding an emergency shedding policy that uses rate-limited token burn to protect critical tier when global errorbudget burn >50%.
2026-03-10 - Design review: Agreed to make floodgate opt-in per-route and add metric for economic cost of failover (tokens rerouted * region-cost-delta).
